Subject: Renewal inquiry — baseline reset + per-token ceiling

Hi Vanessa,

We're preparing our annual renewal and I wanted to flag two things up front that are important for our finance team:

- Our usage has increased ~25% over the past 12 months; current baseline no longer reflects run-rate.
- Budget for next FY is tight. We need a way to reset baseline closer to current run-rate but with some protection against spikes (smoothing/true-up).

Specifically, can Redwood support:
1) a baseline reset to the trailing 3-month average with a 90-day smoothing band (true-up at quarter end),
2) a hard per-token ceiling for year 1 (so we can cap worst-case spend for budgeting), and
3) a renewal uplift cap (we were hoping to avoid >20% uplift YoY).

If you can share a couple of structured options and the expected per-token tiers, procurement will review and we can move to DocuSign.

Thanks,

Maria Gonzalez
Head of Platform
DataSolv Inc.

Hi Maria,

Thanks for the clear ask — this is reasonable and solvable. I put together two options below; I'm looping in Lauren (renewal approvals) and Ben (finance) so we can lock terms quickly.

Option A — Conservative reset
- Baseline stays at current contracted level
- Quarterly true-up; overages billed monthly at standard overage rate
- Per-token ceiling: not available under this option
- Renewal uplift: standard list price (typically 25-40% when usage gaps exist)

Option B — Reset + smoothing (recommended)
- Baseline reset to trailing-3-month average
- 90-day smoothing band (first quarter): overages within first 90 days are eligible for up to 10% forgiveness
- Quarterly true-up thereafter
- Hard per-token ceiling for 12 months (we will propose tiered per-token ceilings for each slab; see attached proposal)
- Renewal uplift cap: max 20% for 12-month renewal if DataSolv commits to a 12-month term and agrees to the adjusted baseline

I've attached a short proposal and a spreadsheet with pricing scenarios for the three-year horizon. If you confirm Option B, we can issue a DocuSign with those clauses and the SOW appendix.

Attachments: Redwood-Proposal-DataSolv-20260901.pdf, pricing-scenarios-vanessa.xlsx

Best,

Vanessa Ortiz

Forwarding DataSolv's ask + my Option B recommendation. Quick points and asks:

- Margin impact: Option B reduces near-term overage revenue but increases commit certainty. On our model, the effective blended ARR impact is neutral if we cap uplift at 20% and lock a 12-month term.
- Finance ask (Ben): can you confirm we are comfortable with a 10% Q1 forgiveness and a locked per-token ceiling for 12 months? I put projected unit economics in pricing-scenarios-vanessa.xlsx.
- Renewal approvals (Lauren): can we approve a one-time exception to the standard renewal uplift policy if they take the 12-month term? I recommend a maximum deviation to 20% uplift cap.
- Commercial sweetener: offering a one-time onboarding credit of $25k if they sign within 10 business days will help close.

If all good, I'll send Option B legally redlined and start the DocuSign flow.
